transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-27
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Evan, Priya, Marco, Leah, Jordan, Marta, ~180 virtual attendees
Deck: slides.redwood.com/all-hands/2027-05-27-playbook (shared)
Postmortem: incidents/redwood-2027-05-kv-cache.md (mentioned)

Summary (auto): Execs walked through a conservative operating posture; prioritized reliability and Dedicated productization; hiring tempo slowed but key roles prioritized.

[00:00] Evan: okay hey everyone, welcome to the all-hands, um thanks for joining on time. I want to start with a short framing — last quarter has been, uh, a mix. strong customer momentum on Dedicated but also a few reliability blips that we did n't fully plan for. so today's goal is alignment: what's our playbook for the next 6–12 weeks and where we re going to focus energy.

[00:32] Priya: quick agenda — metrics, incident recap, product priorities, org changes, and q and a. We'll try to keep the slides light and leave time.

[01:05] Marco: on reliability — the big one was the multi-region KV cache eviction chain that caused token-level latency spikes for some long running chat sessions. root cause was a late refactor in the cache eviction heuristic plus a kernel scheduling corner case on newer recip devices — uh, replaying word 're pip' — on some of the accelerated GPUs. we traced and mitigated with fallback to smaller batch size and quick KV reset.

[01:45] Attendee (virtual): can you repeat that — was it the KV cache or the prefix cache?

[01:52] Marco: sorry yeah, KV cache, the key-value cache we use for decoding; sometimes the transcript tool renders it as K-V cacher.

[02:10] Evan: the incident highlighted two priorities: one, we need stronger canarying for kernel/hardware combos; two, we need a formalized "tide turner" response playbook so teams can triage across runtime, infra and ops quickly.

[03:00] Leah: from GTM perspective, customers noticed the latency during a pilot, we lost some minutes of demos but the sales pipeline is intact — many customers care about predictable latency over raw throughput. so our messaging needs to center reliability and predictable capacity, not just top-qps benchmarks.

[03:35] Priya: product moves — Dedicated: region tagging is ready for internal alpha; that means customers can pin workloads to specific regions with a preview SLA. Private: the on-prem bundle timeline slips by two weeks due to compliance packaging for KMS integration.

[04:10] Marta: finance note — ARR ended the month up 32% YoY, runway unchanged, but we must be conservative on new hiring until we see the impact of the Dedicated upsell pilots. so hiring freeze is partial: prioritize core infra, SEs for Dedicated, and one more security engineer.

[04:45] Jordan: people update — we re moving to a two-tier hiring cadence: critical roles green-lit; non-critical roles staged. we'll share a role priority list and host manager Q&A later this week.

[05:12] Evan: ok let's walk through the priority playbook so it's concrete. slide 6, 'lock the basics' — immediate actions are: 1) 72-hour reliability blitz, 2) freeze large infra merges, 3) double canarying windows for kernels and quant profiles. Marco you'll lead the blitz.

[05:45] Marco: yep, I'll stand up a cross-functional pager team; we'll include runtime, infra, bench and a SE on call. goals: reduce median token latency variance by 30% in production segments and establish an automated KV cache warming check.

[06:20] Attendee (virtual): question — will this change batching profiles?

[06:27] Marco: yes batching profiles are part of the mitigations. we might temporarily move to conservative batching which increases per-token cost but keeps SLOs intact. that'll be a tradeoff we'll own.

[07:00] Priya: on product prioritization: features that materially move enterprise deals get to the front of the queue. that list = Dedicated region SLAs, Private KMS and on-prem quickstart, and rollout controls (canary, rollback, A/B model routing). We will pause lower-impact UX polish for two sprints.

[07:35] Leah: sales playbook tweak — lead with predictable latency and capacity. For pilots we will offer a short Dedicated reservation trial with a rollback credit in the first month. We'll put full details in a one-pager.

[08:05] Marta: financially, small Dedicated reserved deals are fine; large commitments need finance review. build a pricing draft — Priya and Leah, pls sync.

[08:27] Jordan: people questions — what about hiring bands? We re tightening expectations for L4 hiring bar; candidates must clear 3 interviewers including a practical coding/design exercise. Managers will get guidance tomorrow.

[09:00] Evan: now open q and a — keep questions short; if you need a long discussion, book a follow-up.

[09:18] Attendee A: hi — any changes to OKRs?

[09:22] Priya: OKRs will be adjusted to reflect the playbook — reliability ops and Dedicated rollout will be explicit for Platform OKRs, others will be cascaded to squads.

[09:50] Attendee B: will the rollback policy affect customers already on Dedicated?

[09:56] Leah: not retroactively; we will apply the new policy to new pilots and early customers with clear comms. existing customers get a heads-up and a migration offer.

[10:25] Attendee C: are any layoffs planned?

[10:29] Evan: no layoffs. we are recalibrating hiring pace and focusing hires on critical areas; goal is to protect runway while investing in things that unlock revenue.

[11:02] Marco: technical note — the KV issue had a small correlation with quantization profile switching; lab teams will re-run the kernel selection matrix across the most common model families. this could surface other corner cases.

[11:35] Attendee D: will this impact open-source contributions or changes to our community builds?

[11:41] Marco: temporarily we'll gate some low-risk experimental merges until the blitz completes; but core OSS commits remain.

[12:05] Priya: product roadmap highlights — alpha for Dedicated region tagging (June internal), closed beta for Private on-prem quickstart (late June), public docs and pricing (mid-July).

[12:40] Leah: for AE enablement: we ll run a 30-minute GTM briefing next Tuesday and share demo scripts that emphasize degradation patterns and our mitigation story. pls attend if you're customer-facing.

[13:05] Jordan: people ops — reorg note: we re centralizing the SRE reporting into Platform to speed decisions; SRE managers will sit in Platform org, but career ladders unaffected.

[13:38] Attendee E: tiny nit — can we get more transparency on incident timelines? sometimes tickets look closed but the follow-up is thin.

[13:44] Marco: yes — we'll commit to a postmortem publish template and a 72-hour status digest for incidents above severity 2.

[14:10] Evan: financial ask — Marta and finance to model a conservative scenario: two thirds of expected Dedicated uplift delayed three months. we need to know runway impact.

[14:35] Marta: will do; I'll include sensitivity to gross margin improvements from quantization.

[15:00] Attendee F: question on security — does the Private delay affect SOC2/ISO timelines?

[15:06] Priya: SOC2 work is on its own track; KMS integration for private affects the on-prem packaging but shouldn't delay the overall compliance program.

[15:40] Evan: quick culture thing — I hear concern about 'all-hands fatigue' and too many changes. we re aiming for tighter comms and fewer last-minute shifts. Jordan will run a short pulse next week.

[16:05] Jordan: pulse will be anonymous and quick. we want to hear what is working and what's noisy.

[16:30] Priya: ops/engineers — please use the incident channel and the incident template; it's okay to escalate early. we want faster small escalations rather than surprises in all-hands.

[17:05] Attendee G: will we get compensation or recognition for folks who working weekends on the blitz?

[17:10] Evan: absolutely — we'll track on-call hours and offer comp-time and a team bonus if we meet the blitz goals.

[17:45] Priya: final slide: success metrics for the next cycle — reduce P95 latency variance by 30%, improve Dedicated pilot conversion by 15%, close three large enterprise sales anchored on SLA guarantees.

[18:10] Leah: quick plug — product marketing will share a short script for customer conversations and a pilot offer template.

[18:35] Q&A rapid-fire: several questions on docs, who to contact for role clarifications, and where to find the Dedicated pricing draft.

[19:05] Evan: recap — priority playbook, 72-hour blitz, paused non-critical merges, prioritized hires, pricing draft + GTM one-pager. action owners and dates in the sheet we will share.

[19:30] Evan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the playbook doc and calendar invites for the roadmapping sessions. meeting ends.
